dossier.public_summary: The dip changes dramatically from a few hundred ppm to over 2% even within the same data type, and the three usable transits have very different depths. That scattering, seen to be real not a pipeline artifact, means a fixed-size planet transit cannot explain the signal, so it is best explained as noise, detrending residuals or a false association rather than a planet.

reasons.why: Depth is not constant between sectors; sectors.p_constant is far below 0.01.
Change persists within TESS-SPOC (p_constant=2.7668821653522842e-05), so not a calibration/detrending offset between pipelines.

Even single-transit depths scatter wildly. One of only 3 significant events is ~14x deeper than another, which contratio=0.002512 rules out dilution by a standard neighbour and is inconsistent with a constant-depth planet.
reasons.value: p_consistent=2.1648857282514253e-12 chi2=57.3488824874693 dof=3 share_of_top_3=0.989; individual depths 1944 ppm (sigma -4.9) vs 26830 ppm (sigma 4.8)

reasons.why: Low SNR and few events plus a poor density match make the transit-like fit unreliable and do not positively favour a planet when depths/variability dominate.
